🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-09-22 23:00 → 2026-09-23 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **ZK proof of TimesFM 1.0 runs end-to-end on a single machine** — The GKR/WHIR backend proved a 200M-parameter model from input to output in roughly 6.7 minutes, with linear scaling confirmed at 25x the prior benchmark. [tg:tawg:4872]

> **ens-write-v0 classified as requires_live in conformance** — The recompute-kit conformance layer was updated to reflect that ens-write-v0 needs live execution, keeping the uncovered registry accurate and consistent with existing entries. [tg:tawg:4850]

> **Mutation reproducibility locked on permission-consumption-boundary** — Both targeted mutants were independently confirmed on a cold clone at commit 476529e, sharpening what remaining test coverage needs to target. [tg:tawg:4864]

> **Quantum execution evidence repository opened to the public** — A real IBM Quantum run of a Bell circuit, with 256 ordered shots, became openly accessible as a verifiable hardware artifact. [tg:tawg:4857]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### proving

_The ZK proving work reached a new parameter scale milestone and was quickly grounded through a focused technical exchange._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Shipped** an end-to-end proof of the full TimesFM 1.0 model (~200M parameters, 20 layers, real 16-token attention) using the GKR/WHIR backend on a single machine, a concrete step toward proving production-sized AI models under the Trustless AI goal. [tg:tawg:4872]
- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Validated** the scaling behavior by noting that the roughly 6.7-minute proof time aligns closely with the linear extrapolation from the 8M-parameter run, and surfaced targeted follow-up questions about memory and other potential constraints. [tg:tawg:4873]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Resolved** those follow-up questions by reporting that peak memory for the 200M run came in around 1.2 GB — well under earlier estimates — confirming that memory is not the binding constraint at this scale and giving the team clearer headroom for the next size step. [tg:tawg:4874]

### recompute-kit

_Conformance coverage and mutation test verification advanced together, closing open questions from recent merges._

- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Extended** the recompute-kit conformance registry by classifying ens-write-v0 as requires_live in the uncovered module, keeping the conformance layer consistent and accurate for features that depend on live execution. [tg:tawg:4850]
- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Reviewed** the mutation check table in the permission-consumption-boundary conformance module at commit 476529e, identifying the required killers listed for specific mutants and surfacing what test coverage is still needed after the PR #47 merge. [tg:tawg:4862]
- Baby Blue Viper (@babyblueviper1) **Confirmed** on a fresh cold clone at commit 476529e that both described mutants reproduce exactly as expected, and clarified that the identity function's tuple return makes the single identity guard the key requirement, tightening the target for remaining tests. [tg:tawg:4864]

### quantum-execution-evidence

_A new public repository brought verifiable hardware evidence into the open._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Published** the quantum-execution-evidence repository, which preserves a real IBM Quantum run of a 2-qubit Bell circuit on ibm_fez with 256 ordered shots, giving the group an inspectable reference artifact of actual quantum execution that can support future verification and conformance work. [tg:tawg:4857]

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Explore what the confirmed memory headroom implies for the next model size step in the proving pipeline
- Consider how the QEV Bell circuit artifact might serve as a reference pattern for quantum execution conformance
- Investigate whether the mutation killer gaps surfaced in the permission-consumption-boundary module affect related conformance modules

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Review and merge PR #49 (ens-write-v0 requires_live classification in recompute-kit)
- Add or confirm tests that kill the mutants identified in the permission-consumption-boundary mutation table

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A proving milestone became a shared measurement — a run completed, a scaling prediction held, and a concern dissolved into headroom, all resolved through a tight back-and-forth exchange.
>
> When the questions are as sharp as the code, the loop closes itself. Keep the relay going! 🏃
